system.name: EinNet
system.one_liner: a tensor program optimizer that applies derivation-based transformations over tensor algebra expressions to discover new operators and schedules

components.name: Conv3x3
components.role: 3x3 convolution predefined operator, input to the optimization

components.name: DLT
components.role: eOperator for data-layout transformation, discovered by intra-expression derivation to help convert Conv into Matmul form

components.name: Matmul
components.role: predefined matrix-multiplication operator that Conv3x3/Conv1x1 are transformed into

components.name: OffsetReduce
components.role: eOperator that reduces offset tensors, replacing part of Conv3x3's computation

components.name: DLT+Concat
components.role: fused eOperator merging the data-layout transform and concatenation of the two weight tensors

components.name: Split
components.role: splits the fused Matmul output back into two equivalent outputs

components.name: OffsetReduce+Relu
components.role: fused eOperator merging OffsetReduce and Relu via expression fusion

components.name: Conv
components.role: baseline convolution over an h,w,c input and r,s,c weight, the starting point optimized in panels (b) and (c)

components.name: DLT
components.role: splits/reshapes the weight tensor along kernel dimensions r and s ahead of the Matmul-based rewrite

components.name: Matmul
components.role: matrix multiplication applied to each split weight slice against the input
components.container: (iii) Transform Conv to Matmul with OffsetReduce

components.name: OffsetReduce
components.role: reduces the per-slice Matmul outputs into the final convolution result
components.container: (iii) Transform Conv to Matmul with OffsetReduce

components.name: DLT
components.role: flattens the small r,s,c weight tensor into a vector for the im2col-style Matmul

components.name: OffsetConcat
components.role: concatenates the duplicated, offset copies of the input tensor (the classic im2col step)

components.name: Matmul
components.role: matrix multiplication of the concatenated duplicated input with the flattened weight vector
components.container: (iii) Transform Conv to Matmul using im2col algorithm

fused with Relu via expression fusion

content.key_idea: EinNet automatically discovers non-obvious tensor-program rewrites, such as transforming a Conv3x3 into a Matmul plus a new OffsetReduce eOperator and fusing adjacent operators, that go beyond classic optimizations like im2col.
content.reading_order: Left to right across three panels: (a) a three-step before/after derivation of a small subgraph, (b) EinNet's own convolution-to-Matmul rewrite via OffsetReduce, (c) the classic im2col rewrite shown for comparison.

tensor cube outlines/fills for the weight and input tensors in panels (b) and (c)

encoding.color_means: red-filled boxes mark eOperators EinNet automatically discovers (DLT, OffsetReduce, DLT+Concat, OffsetReduce+Relu, OffsetConcat); tan/orange boxes mark predefined operators (Conv, Matmul, Relu, Add); pale-yellow circles mark named tensors; small red squares inside output tiles mark values produced by an eOperator
encoding.emphasis: red eOperator boxes visually pop against the tan predefined-operator boxes across all three panels, and thick gray arrows between the (i)/(ii)/(iii) steps of panel (a) narrate its two-step derivation
reusable_patterns: side-by-side comparison of the paper's rewrite against a well-known baseline technique (im2col)
small tensor-cube glyphs annotated with dimension letters (h,w,c,r,s)
weaknesses: very high text/shape density makes the figure hard to read at reduced size

EINNET transforms a Conv3x3 to a Matmul and an eOperator (OffsetReduce)

summary: This figure compares three optimization examples for convolution. Panel (a) walks a small subgraph through EinNet's process: an original Conv3x3/Conv1x1/Relu/Add graph is first rewritten by intra-expression derivation into DLT and Matmul operators plus a new OffsetReduce eOperator, then by inter-expression derivation into a fused DLT+Concat and OffsetReduce+Relu. Panel (b) shows EinNet's own convolution rewrite in more detail: the weight tensor is split along kernel dimensions r and s (via DLT), each slice is matrix-multiplied, and OffsetReduce combines the results. Panel (c) shows the classic im2col rewrite for comparison, which instead duplicates the input tensor for each kernel position and concatenates it (OffsetConcat) before a single Matmul. Red boxes mark EinNet's automatically discovered eOperators throughout, contrasted with tan predefined operators.
summary_zh: 该图对比三种卷积优化：(a)EinNet对子图先做表达式内推导得DLT/Matmul/OffsetReduce，再做表达式间推导融合；(b)展示该重写细节；(c)展示经典im2col做法作对比。
notes: layout-proposal: side-by-side derivation triptych — three side-by-side panels, each a short chain of small operator-graph diagrams, comparing EinNet's found rewrites (a, b) against the classic im2col baseline (c).
